title: Positive Expiratory Pressure (PEP) and Continuous High-frequency Oscillation (CHFO) on Lung RECRUITment Using Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) - The PEP-RECRUIT Study
official: Effect of Continuous High-frequency Oscillation (CHFO) and Continuous Positive Expiratory Pressure (CPEP) Therapy on Lung RECRUITment Using Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) - The PEP-RECRUIT Study
summary: This single-center observational study aims to assess the effects of continuous high-frequency oscillation (CHFO) and continuous positive expiratory pressure (CPEP) therapy on lung recruitment using electrical impedance tomography (EIT) in spontaneously breathing patients admitted to the intensive care unit.

interventions.name: Continuous high-frequency oscillation (CHFO) and continuous positive expiratory pressure (CPEP) therapy

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients who require pulmonary expansion and airway clearing as per clinical indication
* Patients who provide valid informed consent according to local regulations
* PaO2/FiO2 \< 200 mmHg at inclusion
* Patient on the Airway Care Score (ACS) \< 7

Exclusion Criteria:

* Refuse to participate
* Age \< 18 years
* Hemodynamic instability, defined as systolic arterial pressure \< 90 mmHg or mean pressure \< 60 mmHg
* Contraindication to using an EIT (i.e., pacemaker or defibrillator)
* Inability to properly position the EIT device for anatomical reasons
